claims.text: To enable debug mode, open the agent in Builder, toggle Debug mode in the preview pane, and run the agent; multi-turn chat is supported.
In the debug trace, green indicates success and red indicates error, and the trace persists across panel open and close.
The debug trace exposes inputs, including referenced memory and variables, and outputs, including raw tool and LLM responses.
The effective debugging workflow is to filter to only show errors, open the failing step, compare inputs against outputs, and iterate with Try Again or Reset Preview.
Failure category 1 is instruction-following failures: wrong tools planned, ignored instructions, and a sloppy final answer.
Failure category 2 is retrieval and context-selection failures: the right tool runs but returns wrong or missing results, such as document not found when it exists.
Failure category 3 is action and integration failures: HTTP errors, validation errors, partial writes, and timeouts.
Failure category 4 is trigger and scheduling failures: the agent never runs, runs at the wrong time, or runs on the wrong content.
Failure category 5 is UI and configuration issues: buttons not working, save failures, and permissions problems.
Too much memory leads to slower, more expensive runs with wandering answers, while too little memory creates brittle agents that forget constraints or prior results.
Memory options are all previous steps for short flows or complex reasoning, only the immediate previous step as the default for formatting and cleanup, and no memory for independent operations.
Model selection strategy is to use small and fast models for simple transforms and reserve larger models only where reasoning clearly benefits the outcome.
Partners should use the Glean Help Center 'Debug your agent' official guide and practice with live labs on a demo tenant to build hands-on debugging expertise.
The Advanced Agent Debugging training equips technical partner engineers and architects with tools, frameworks, and hands-on techniques to troubleshoot effectively and escalate intelligently.
The debugging journey covers the agent execution mental model, the debugging toolbox, the failure taxonomy, and escalation.
Debugging aims to find the root cause rather than just the symptoms.
SRV-204 covers trace-driven debugging, issue isolation, and clean escalation packages.
The Advanced Agent Debugging playbook helps partners resolve customer issues faster, increase trust in production agents, and provide clear, actionable escalations back to Glean.
